name: Cellulose
notes: A genome is capable of cellulose degradation if it encodes at least one endo-acting cellulase, one exo-acting cellobiohydrolase, and one β-glucosidase. LPMOs [AA9, AA10, AA16] provide an oxidative bonus that enhances but is not essential for cellulose degradation.

name: Hemicellulose
notes: For a genome to have hemicellulose degradation capability, it should encode: at least one backbone hydrolase, one side-chain/esterase, and optionally an LPMO for enhanced activity.

name: Starch
notes: For a genome to have starch degradation capability, it should encode: at least one amylolytic hydrolase [GH13, GH14, GH15, GH57, GH97, GH119, GH126, GH133] and optionally an LPMO [AA13] for oxidative enhancement.

name: Pectin
notes: For a genome to have pectin degradation capability, it should encode: at least one backbone-cleaving hydrolase or lyase, one debranching or accessory enzyme, and one esterase for de-methylation or de-acetylation.

name: Lignin
notes: For a genome to have lignin degradation capability, it should encode: at least one oxidative polymer attack enzyme [AA1, mco, AA2, dyp] and one redox support enzyme [AA3_1, AA3_2, AA5_1, AA8] to drive oxidative depolymerization.
gene_ids: AA1, mco, AA2, dyp, AA3_2, AA5_1, AA8, AA3_1

name: Lignin and Aromatic Compounds
notes: Multicopper oxidases use copper-dependent electron transfer reactions to oxidize phenolic and aromatic compounds; laccases oxidize phenolic and lignin-derived compounds using molecular oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor; and lignin peroxidases use hydrogen peroxide-dependent reactions to oxidize lignin and other recalcitrant aromatic compounds.

name: Sucrose
notes: Presence of sucrose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to degrade, transform, or utilize sucrose, a common plant-derived sugar that can fuel rhizosphere microbial activity.

name: Mannose
notes: Presence of mannose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize mannose-containing carbohydrates, supporting turnover of plant- and microbial-derived sugar compounds.

name: Galactose
notes: Presence of galactose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize galactose derived from plant polysaccharides, glycoproteins, or other organic matter inputs.

name: Fucose
notes: Presence of fucose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize fucose-containing sugars, supporting transformation of plant-, microbial-, or mucilage-derived carbon compounds.

name: Xylose
notes: Presence of xylose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize xylose, a major hemicellulose-derived sugar, linking plant polymer breakdown to downstream carbon metabolism.

name: Fructose
notes: Presence of fructose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize fructose and related plant-derived sugars that can support rhizosphere microbial growth and carbon turnover.

name: Arabinose
notes: Presence of arabinose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize arabinose, a common component of hemicellulose and pectin-derived plant carbohydrates.

name: Rhamnose
notes: Presence of rhamnose metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to utilize rhamnose-containing plant or microbial polysaccharides, supporting turnover of complex sugar inputs.

name: Pyruvate
notes: Pyruvate conversion to acetyl-CoA occurs via one of three enzyme complexes: pyruvate dehydrogenase [K00163], 2-oxoacid ferredoxin oxidoreductase [K00174], or formate-acetyltransferase [K00656]. Presence of any indicates potential for acetyl-CoA formation.

name: Acetate
notes: Acetate production can occur via the phosphate acetyltransferase–acetate kinase route [K00625 & K00925] or alternative ligase [K01905] or hydrolase [K01067] pathways. Either route yields acetate from acetyl-CoA.

name: Lactate
notes: Lactate formation can occur through L-lactate dehydrogenases [K00016, K00101] or D-lactate variants [K03778, K03777]. Presence of any indicates capacity for pyruvate reduction to lactate.

name: Butyrate
notes: Butyrate formation proceeds via phosphate butyryltransferase [K00634] coupled with either butyrate kinase [K00929] or medium-chain acyl-CoA synthetase [K01896]. Both steps are required for full conversion.

name: Propionate
notes: Propionate formation requires both propionate kinase [K19697] and propionate CoA-transferase [K01026] for CoA-dependent conversion of intermediates to propionate.

name: Alcohol
notes: For a genome to have alcohol conversion capability, it should encode: at least one alcohol dehydrogenase or related enzyme involved in ethanol and higher-alcohol interconversion.

name: CO2 Fixation
notes: For a genome to have CO₂ fixation capability via the acetyl-CoA pathway, it should encode: the complete CODH/ACS complex [cdhA, cdhB, cdhC, cdhD, and cdhE subunits], which together catalyze CO₂ reduction to acetyl-CoA.

name: CH4 Oxidation
rule: HMM@pmoa_actinobacteria_chloroflexota | HMM@pmoa_alpha_1 | HMM@pmoa_alpha_2 | HMM@pmoa_crenothrix | HMM@pmoa_gamma | HMM@pmoa_methyl_eth | HMM@pmoa_methylomirabilis | HMM@pmoa_verr
notes: For a genome to have CH₄ oxidation capability, it must encode at least one methane monooxygenase complex [pMMO or sMMO], which catalyzes the conversion of methane to methanol — the key diagnostic step of methanotrophy in soils.

name: Nitrate Loss
notes: Nitrate transformation represents the combined capacity for nitrate [NO₃⁻] reduction to nitrite [NO₂⁻] and subsequent nitrite reduction to nitric oxide [NO]. It integrates both the Nar/Nap [nitrate reductase] and Nir [nitrite reductase] steps, capturing the overall microbial potential to transform fertilizer-derived nitrate into reduced nitrogen intermediates.

name: Urea Degradation
notes: Urea hydrolysis requires the full urease enzyme complex, composed of subunits ureA [K01430], ureB [K01429], and ureC [K01428]. All three genes are needed to complete urea transformation to ammonium and CO₂.

name: Aerobic Ammonium Oxidation
notes: Ammonium oxidation [NH₃ to NO₂⁻] requires both ammonia monooxygenase [any of K28504, K10944, K10945, or K10946] and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase [K10535]. Presence of both indicates this process.

name: N2 Fixation
notes: Nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric N₂ to ammonium through the nitrogenase enzyme complex. Functional capacity is indicated by the presence of all subunits for either the Mo-nitrogenase [nif] or the V-nitrogenase [vnf] system, as either complete complex can catalyze N₂ reduction.

name: Aerobic Ammonium Oxidation
notes: Aerobic ammonium oxidation converts ammonia to nitrite through sequential reactions catalyzed by ammonia monooxygenase and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase. Presence of one ammonia monooxygenase subunit set and hydroxylamine oxidoreductase indicates this capability.

name: Aerobic Nitrite Oxidation
notes: Aerobic nitrate oxidation [nitrite oxidation] is the second step of nitrification, where nitrite is oxidized to nitrate by the NXR complex [nxrAB] under oxic conditions, completing the conversion of reduced nitrogen to its most oxidized form.

name: Anaerobic Ammonium Oxidation
notes: Anammox requires nitrite → NO [nirK or nirS], hydrazine synthesis via HZS [hzsA/B/C], and hydrazine oxidation to N₂ by HDH.

name: NO3 to NO2
notes: Nitrate reduction to nitrite can occur through either the membrane-bound Nar system [K00370, K00371] or the periplasmic Nap system [K02567, K02568]. Either system completes the nitrate transformation step.

name: NO2 to NO
notes: Nitrite reduction to nitric oxide [NO] is carried out by either NirS [K00368] or NirK [K15864]. Presence of either gene indicates capacity for nitrate/nitrite reduction in denitrification.

name: NO to N2O
notes: The conversion of nitric oxide [NO] to nitrous oxide [N₂O] is catalyzed by nitric oxide reductase, encoded by norB [K04561] in bacteria or CYP55 [K15877] in fungi. Presence of either gene indicates the capacity to perform this denitrification step

name: N2O to N2
notes: The reduction of nitrous oxide [N₂O] to dinitrogen gas [N₂] is catalyzed by nitrous oxide reductase [nosZ, K00376]. Presence of this gene indicates the potential for the final step of denitrification, converting greenhouse gas N₂O into inert atmospheric N₂.

name: DNRA, NO3 to NH4
notes: DNRA reduces nitrate to ammonium through a two-step process: nitrate reduction via Nar or Nap systems, followed by nitrite reduction via Nrf or Nir enzymes. Presence of one nitrate reductase system and one nitrite reductase system indicates DNRA capability.

name: Sulfur Transport

name: β-D-glucosidase
notes: Presence of any β-D-glucosidase gene indicates potential for microbial hydrolysis of cellulose-derived oligosaccharides into glucose, reflecting active carbon cycling and decomposition processes in soil.

name: β-D-xylosidase
notes: Presence of any β-D-xylosidase gene indicates potential for microbial breakdown of hemicellulosic xylans into xylose, contributing to carbon turnover from plant residues in soil.

name: Arylsulphatase
notes: Presence of an arylsulfatase gene indicates microbial capacity to hydrolyze sulfate esters, releasing inorganic sulfur for plant and microbial use in soil systems.

name: N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminidase
notes: Presence of any N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminidase [NAGase] gene indicates potential for microbial chitin degradation and turnover of fungal or insect-derived organic matter, contributing to soil nitrogen cycling.

name: Phosphatase
notes: Presence of any phosphatase gene indicates potential for microbial hydrolysis of organic phosphorus compounds, releasing inorganic phosphate available for plant uptake.

name: Leucine aminopeptidase
notes: Presence of any leucine aminopeptidase gene indicates potential for microbial degradation of peptides and proteins, contributing to nitrogen mineralization and organic matter turnover in soil.

name: cellobiohydrolase
notes: Presence of any cellobiohydrolase gene indicates potential for microbial cleavage of crystalline cellulose into cellobiose, representing a key step in cellulose degradation and carbon release from plant material.

name: α-1,4-glucosidase
notes: Presence of any α-glucosidase gene indicates potential for microbial hydrolysis of α-linked glucosides such as maltose and starch, contributing to carbon mobilization from easily degradable carbohydrates in soil.

name: Peroxidase
notes: Presence of a peroxidase gene indicates microbial capacity to oxidatively degrade lignin and other complex organic compounds, contributing to soil organic matter transformation and stabilization.

name: phenoloxidase
notes: Presence of any phenoloxidase [laccase] gene indicates microbial ability to oxidize phenolic compounds and participate in lignin degradation, influencing soil organic matter stability and humification.

name: Auxin [IAA] Biosynthesis
notes: Presence of auxin biosynthesis genes from the IPA, IAM, TAM, or IAN pathways indicates microbial potential to synthesize indole-3-acetic acid [IAA] or IAA precursors from tryptophan-derived substrates. These pathways may influence root architecture, lateral root formation, root hair development, and plant–microbe interactions in the rhizosphere.

name: Auxin [IAA] Inactivation
notes: Presence of iaaL indicates microbial potential to conjugate free indole-3-acetic acid [IAA] to lysine, forming IAA-Lys. This process can reduce the pool of bioactive IAA and may regulate auxin availability, root development, and plant–microbe signaling in the rhizosphere.

name: ACC Deaminase
notes: Presence of ACC deaminase [acdS] indicates microbial potential to degrade 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate [ACC], reducing plant ethylene levels and promoting root growth under stress conditions.

name: Cytokinin Biosynthesis
notes: Presence of cytokinin biosynthesis genes indicates microbial potential to produce cytokinin precursors, which may influence plant cell division, root–shoot growth balance, nutrient signaling, and plant–microbe interactions.

name: Cytokinin Degradation
notes: Presence of cytokinin degradation genes indicates microbial potential to break down cytokinins, which may regulate cytokinin availability and influence plant growth signaling in the rhizosphere.

name: Gibberellins
notes: Presence of gibberellin biosynthesis genes [cps, ks, cyp701A, cyp88A] indicates microbial potential to produce gibberellin intermediates that stimulate plant growth, germination, and root elongation.

name: Phenolics
notes: Presence of phenolic metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to transform phenolic or aromatic compounds involved in plant signaling, defense responses, and rhizosphere chemical interactions.

name: Sugar Compatible Solutes [Trehalose]
notes: Presence of trehalose biosynthesis or metabolism genes indicates microbial potential to produce or cycle trehalose, an osmoprotectant that helps maintain cellular water balance under drought, salinity, or osmotic stress.

name: Sugar Compatible Solutes [Mannitol]
notes: Presence of mannitol biosynthesis genes indicates microbial potential to produce mannitol, a sugar alcohol osmoprotectant that supports cellular protection under drought, salinity, or osmotic stress.

name: Sugar Compatible Solutes [Mannosylglycerate]
notes: Presence of mannosylglycerate biosynthesis genes indicates microbial potential to produce mannosylglycerate, a compatible solute that supports osmotic and stress tolerance.

name: Non-Sugar Compatible Solutes
notes: Presence of non-sugar compatible solute biosynthesis genes indicates microbial potential to produce osmoprotectants such as proline or glycerol, supporting cellular water balance under drought, salinity, or osmotic stress.

name: Methyl-Related Compatible Solutes Biosynthesis
notes: Presence of methyl-related compatible solute biosynthesis genes indicates microbial potential to produce glycine betaine or related osmoprotectants that help maintain cellular water balance under drought, salinity, or osmotic stress in agricultural soils.

name: Oxidative Stress Response
notes: Presence of oxidative stress response genes indicates microbial potential to detoxify reactive oxygen species through catalase–peroxidase, superoxide dismutase, glutathione biosynthesis, or NADH peroxidase, supporting survival under oxidative stress in agricultural soils.

name: Exopolysaccharide [EPS]
notes: Presence any of EPS biosynthesis genes [e.g., exo, alg, psl, pss] indicates microbial potential to produce extracellular polysaccharides that promote soil aggregation, water retention, and plant–microbe interactions such as rhizobial nodulation and biofilm stability. These traits enhance soil structure and drought resilience in agricultural ecosystems.

name: Biofilms
notes: Presence of alginate, Psl, or PGA/ICA matrix biosynthesis genes indicates microbial capacity for biofilm formation, enhancing root colonization, surface adhesion, and drought resilience. Biofilm production supports rhizosphere stability, moisture retention, and plant–microbe symbiosis in agricultural soils.

name: Copper Detox

name: Arsenic Detox
